_doc: THE JUDGEMENT half of the mock-compare rig (docs/design/verifying-against-a-mock.md).
mock_compare_shot.gd is deterministic — it crops, paints and lays out exactly what is written here
and never guesses a rect, a colour or a scale. Everything a human had to LOOK at to decide lives in
this file: which mock, which pixels of it are the element, which pixels beside it are genuinely
empty ground, and which patches of it are flat field.
Adding a region: open the mock, measure the element's FACE rect (the drawn sheet, NOT its shadow —
the shadow is the thing being measured and must sit outside the rect), then measure how far the
clean ground really runs on each side before the next element, the canvas edge, or any painted
detail. `clean` is that window; the tool derives `real_ground` per side from it and the profiler
refuses to report past it. Overstating `clean` by 6px is how a profile reports a serene 0.000 and
gets believed.
rect format is [x, y, w, h] in the mock's OWN pixels.
`encloses` names regions the mock draws INSIDE this one's sheet (its info bar holds a bag well).
It exempts exactly that pair from the clean-window and field-patch guards, which exist for an
element BESIDE another: a container's own contents are never crossed by a profile stepping OUT
from its face, and the enclosed element's field genuinely IS the enclosing sheet. The guard
verifies the claim — an `encloses` name whose face is not contained in this one's fails.
A MOCK MAY HAVE NO REGIONS AT ALL. Some concept art cannot be measured this way — an element
painted directly onto busy art has no flat ground beside it, and this rig divides every sample by
ONE field luma. Such a mock is still registered (it is the durable record of what was approved and
what its rects are) but declares `field_candidates` instead of regions: the patches that were tried
as field and failed. test_mock_targets.py re-measures them, so 'there is no flat ground here' is a
checked claim rather than a remembered one.

note: THE STOREFRONT the shop is drawn from since 2026-07-30 (owner: 'use the market stall as it is'):
concept A of shop_screen_variations_v1. A scalloped coral/cream awning, a slate signboard hung on
two cords, four slate plank shelves against a pale-meadow paper wall, the goods standing on them,
cream amount tags propped at their base and action-green price buttons pinned to the shelf lips.
It REPLACES shop_dialog_v3 (the unified cream sheet of sage offer cards); that design's one
region, `shop_card`, retired with the card it measured — the storefront has no offer card any
more, so there was nothing left for the adapter to build.
IT CARRIES NO REGIONS, AND CANNOT. This rig divides every sample by ONE field luma, and this
painting has no flat ground to give: the wall is painted with a broad vignette AND every shelf lip
drops a tinted shadow across it, so the quiet-looking stretches are gradients. Measured with the
rule-9 diagnostic (mock_profile.flat_range, limit 12, where meadow_board's own empty sky reads
4.7-7.9) the seven `field_candidates` read 42.9, 97.3, 90.2, 146.2, 30.9, 84.1 and 113.2 — the
last of those is the shelf plank's own lit face beside a price tag, which is the only ground other
than the wall that anything on this mock sits on.
ONE patch on the whole mock does measure flat: the wall immediately right of the signboard,
[840,372,120,68], reads 11.2. It is deliberately NOT registered as a field, because nothing is
beside it — the sign is to its left and the stall post to its right — and rule 7 says do not
report past the clean ground you actually have. It is recorded here so the claim above is bounded
rather than absolute.
WHAT THE MOCK WAS USED FOR INSTEAD is everything that needs no ground: the shelf bands were read
off the PNG by scanning for the slate rows beside the left post (plank tops 672 / 1120 / ~1455 /
1790; lit faces 101 then 67 px; lips 57 then 51), and every metric on
engine/scripts/ui/market_stall.gd is one of those measurements over the mock's own 1080 width. The
MATERIAL is not this mock's to give either way — the stall is built from the shared cut-paper
panel, whose edge is fitted on meadow_board and guarded by engine/tests/smooth_paper_tests.gd.

meadow_board.note: the board screen the whole cut-paper skin was drawn from: flat sky field, one light from the upper left

note: THE APPROVED TOP-CHROME CONCEPT (variant A, 'furniture only'): the home screen with its wallet
pills, level chip and settings gear restyled into the nav row's cut-paper language and the leaf
field left exactly as it ships. It is what the wallet/gear pass was built to.
IT CARRIES NO REGIONS, AND CANNOT. Every piece of its furniture sits directly on the dense leaf
field — the variant's whole point — so there is no flat ground anywhere near it, and this rig
infers darkening from a luma ratio against ONE field colour. Measured with the rule-9 diagnostic
(mock_profile.flat_range: blur, then the worst max-min over a 24px tile), the widest stretches of
bare ground beside the top row read 77 to 131 against a limit of 12 — the meadow_board mock's own
declared sky patches read 4.7 to 7.9. A `field` patch cut from any of them would put the leaf
texture into the background every darkening on the sheet is then divided by. `field_candidates`
below are those patches; test_mock_targets.py re-measures them, so this claim is checked and not
remembered.
WHAT WAS MEASURED INSTEAD. The pill's SHADOW was fitted against `wallet_acorn` / `wallet_water` on
meadow_board — the same wallet, painted by the same hand under the same upper-left light, on flat
sky — which is the comparison this rig can actually make. Variant A was used for the judgements
that need no ground at all: which paper role goes behind which currency, and the face rects below.
A's FACE RECTS, for anyone measuring its colours: level chip [22,29,104,104] · water pill
[948,113,116,113]. Its pill faces are OVER-SATURATED against the tab family it was asked to join
(water 59%, coin 33%, acorn 38% mean saturation, against the shipped tabs' 7-30%), so the build
chalks the roles through NavBar.chalk instead of sampling A's own pixels.

next_unlock.note: the NEXT UNLOCK strip's own mock, at OUR canvas size (so its px are ours 1:1). Same scene light as meadow_board — measured, its band's shadow side reads 0.383 against that mock's nav tabs' 0.388 — but a different sky tint, so the two mocks' regions can never share a sheet.

nav_home.note: the LEFTMOST tab — the only one in the row with real sky to its LEFT (24px, to the canvas edge). Its right side runs into Board's gap 10px away, and the info card crosses the full width 20px above it, so `clean` opens only 5px above the tab. The row's paper runs off the canvas bottom, hence bleed.

nav_shop.note: the RIGHTMOST tab — 37px of real sky to its RIGHT. Pair it with nav_home: one carries the lit edge, the other the shadow edge, and no single symmetric ring is both.

infobar_tray.note: the INFO BAR — the wide cream sheet the board's own info tray is the counterpart of. It sits on plain sky with 52px of clean ground to its LEFT (to the canvas edge) and 51px to its RIGHT, and almost none above or below: the board frame's own dark bottom edge closes in 4px above it and the nav row's tiles begin 10px below, so neither vertical profile may be read. It ENCLOSES infobar_bag — the mock draws that bag well ON this sheet — which is why the clean-window and field-patch guards skip that one pair; a container's contents are not a neighbour, and a profile that steps OUT from this face never crosses them. TWO THINGS THE MOCK DOES NOT SHOW, and which this region is therefore no authority on: this sheet FLOATS (its bottom edge is drawn, at y=1541, with the tab row a separate row below it) and its sides are straight — measured, the left edge holds x=52 and the right 879-880 down its whole run, a lean of ~0.01 against the nav tabs' 0.031. Ours bleeds and flares because the owner asked for one bottom row, not two. The material is what this region is for.

infobar_bag.note: the BAG WELL — the mock's only free-standing square paper button, and the counterpart of the board's own Bag well. It does NOT sit on sky: the mock draws it INSIDE the cream info-bar sheet, so this region's field is that sheet's cream (250,236,217) and it cannot share a sheet with the nav/wallet regions (their sky is far outside FIELD_TOLERANCE). Ground is tight and asymmetric: 40px of clean cream to its LEFT, but only 11px to its RIGHT before the info bar's own edge, 5px above and 7px below before that sheet's edge shading — which is exactly the shadow side, so the right-hand profile must not be read past ~10px. The mock's face is 161x128; ours ships SQUARE, and the aspect is the board's layout choice rather than the material's, so the rig builds ours at the mock's own box (face_h). The mock's bag also carries a '0/6' count the board draws as a separate Label outside the shared builder — not reproduced here, and it touches no edge.

wallet_water.note: the LEFTMOST wallet pill. 65px of clean sky to its left (the level star ends at x=147 and its own shadow a few px later), 22px above, 20px below before the giver cards. Its right side is 11px from the coin pill and half of that is shadow, so `clean` stops 8px out.

wallet_acorn.note: the RIGHTMOST wallet pill — 20px of real sky to its RIGHT before the canvas edge, which is the only pill edge in the row where the shadow side falls on plain sky. Its LEFT gets only 4px: the coin pill's face ends 11px away and its own right-side shadow runs ~10px into that gap, so there is barely any clean ground on this side at all — measured with `clean` opened to 8px, the profile turned back UPWARDS at 6-8px, which was the neighbour's shadow, not this pill's. The mock draws an acorn; the game's id for that currency is `gem`.

unlock_band.note: the NEXT UNLOCK band — one smooth rounded sheet FLOATING on the sky (it touches no screen edge, so no bleed and no flare). Its useful ground is SIDEWAYS: 26px of clean sky to its LEFT and 26px to its RIGHT, both running to the canvas edge, which is exactly the lit/shadow pair the shared material was fitted against. Neither vertical profile may be read far — the wallet pills' own shadows close in 7px above it and the giver cards begin 12px below — so `clean` stops there. It ENCLOSES unlock_track: the mock draws the bar's well INTO this sheet, so that one is not a neighbour and its field is this sheet's cream, not the sky. No native_px: unlike `well` and `tray` this element derives EVERY length from its own height (UnlockBar.surface_cp), so the mock's box scales it whole.

unlock_track.note: the BAR — a recessed cream well with a green capsule lying in it. It does NOT sit on sky: the mock cuts it into the band's own cream (251,236,218), so rule 16 applies and this region cannot share a sheet with unlock_band (the field tolerance refuses it anyway). Ground is generous vertically (41px of clean band above, 35px below) and tight along the bar: the LEVEL 3 line ends 19px to its left and the 67% read-out starts 16px to its right, so `clean` opens 14px and 12px. What the sideways profile measures here is the LIP, not a cast shadow — a well is sunk, it throws nothing outward — and the fill's own head shadow lives INSIDE the element, where mock_profile.py's `--probe` is the honest instrument.
